record.summary: In this parallel-group trial of male high school students meeting CDC-1994 CFS criteria, a 12-week supervised aerobic exercise intervention was compared with a CFS control group. Total, physical, and mental fatigue scores improved significantly in the exercise group and were significantly better than in the control group at 12 weeks, all p < 0.001. Nail 3-nitrotyrosine also decreased after exercise, p < 0.05, but figure-only numerical values were unavailable.

extraction_metadata.extractor_notes: Table 2 provides means ± SD but does not state cell-specific sample sizes; baseline n=23 per trial arm and 12-week n=20 for EI and n=23 for CFS were taken from participant completion reporting. HCs are a non-randomized reference group and were retained only in baseline_demographics. 3-NT numerical data are available only in Figure 1, so arm means and SDs are not reported. Metabolomics section reports 67,432 extracted peaks, 44,556 retained peaks, 1,411 qualified substances, 20 baseline differential metabolites, and 21 post-intervention differential metabolites; no per-metabolite quantitative arm summaries were provided in this section.

record.summary: In this parallel-group trial of male high school students meeting CDC-1994 CFS criteria, a 12-week supervised aerobic exercise intervention was compared with a CFS control group. Total, physical, and mental fatigue scores improved significantly in the exercise group and were significantly better than in the control group at 12 weeks, all p < 0.001. Nail 3-nitrotyrosine also decreased after exercise, p < 0.05, but figure-only numerical values were unavailable.

extraction_metadata.extractor_notes: Table 2 provides means ± SD but does not state cell-specific sample sizes; baseline n=23 per trial arm and 12-week n=20 for EI and n=23 for CFS were taken from participant completion reporting. HCs are a non-randomized reference group and were retained only in baseline_demographics. 3-NT numerical data are available only in Figure 1, so arm means and SDs are not reported. Metabolomics section reports 67,432 extracted peaks, 44,556 retained peaks, 1,411 qualified substances, 20 baseline differential metabolites, and 21 post-intervention differential metabolites; no per-metabolite quantitative arm summaries were provided in this section.

record.summary: In this double-blind randomized trial of female adults with Fukuda-defined ME/CFS, a nine-month oral ImmunoVita beta-glucan supplement was compared with placebo. HADS anxiety, depression, and total scores and most SF-36 domains showed no statistically significant within-group changes; social role functioning improved significantly only in the placebo group (p = 0.0131).

record.summary: In 51 adult women with Fukuda-defined ME/CFS, a 9-month oral beta-glucan, vitamin D3, vitamin B6, and zinc supplement was compared with placebo. The active group showed a statistically significant within-group improvement in FIS-40 cognitive fatigue at 36 weeks (p=0.0338), but other FIS-40 and PSQI outcomes were not statistically significant in the supplied section. The reported daytime-dysfunction narrative conflicts with the Table 3 active-arm p-value.

extraction_metadata.extractor_notes: Source section ends during the introduction of Table 4; anxiety/depression numeric rows are not supplied. Table 3 reports active-arm daytime dysfunction p=0.7963, while the prose states p=0.0131; preserve both as reported. Baseline daytime dysfunction differed between groups (p=0.0015).

record.summary: This open-label randomized trial evaluated vitamin D replacement therapy guidance plus alfacalcidol versus alfacalcidol alone in adults with ME/CFS following COVID-19 infection or vaccination and low vitamin D levels. record.summary: This open-label randomized trial tested comprehensive vitamin D replacement therapy guidance, including 25 μg daily vitamin D3, dietary guidance, sun exposure recommendations, and exercise therapy, against alfacalcidol alone in adults with ME/CFS following COVID-19 infection or vaccination and vitamin D insufficiency or deficiency. At Week 12, the intervention group had a reported mean reduction of 6.7 ME/CFS symptoms, while the control group showed minimal change; the paper reports significantly greater symptom improvement and vitamin D increase with the intervention.

source_design_and_timing.design: Placebo-controlled, randomized, double-blind, balanced crossover clinical trial.
source_design_and_timing.washout: Two months, intended to prevent residual or carry-over effects.
source_design_and_timing.crossover_sequence: Half received placebo first and half GAA first; sequence described as balanced.
source_design_and_timing.assessment_timing: Assessments before and after three months of supplementation; Figure 1 depicts sampling at months 0, 3, 5, and 8.
source_design_and_timing.population: Women older than 18 years fulfilling 1994 CDC CFS criteria.
source_design_and_timing.blinding: Double-blind; placebo was cellulose.
source_design_and_timing.ethics: Institutional Review Board approval Ref. No. 878/13-EUTC:03; informed consent; Declaration of Helsinki.
source_design_and_timing.carryover: Washout was included to prevent residual/carry-over effects; no separate quantitative carryover analysis was reported.

source_dose_and_delivery.lifestyle_instructions: Maintain usual lifestyle and dietary intake; no dietary supplements during the study.
source_dose_and_delivery.rationale: Dose selected to produce the desired effect, such as increased plasma creatine, with minimum side effects based on prior work.

exercise_protocol.strength: Bilateral maximal isometric voluntary knee-extensor strength; two efforts per leg; better effort recorded; cumulative total used.
exercise_protocol.endurance: Incremental treadmill walk/run beginning at 5 km/h, increasing by 1 km/h each minute until maximal symptom-tolerated level.
exercise_protocol.actigraphy: Daily activity intensity, duration, and active energy expenditure recorded and averaged over study duration.
exercise_protocol.familiarization: Preliminary clinic visit two weeks before study commencement.

source_limitations: Only 14 of 21 randomized participants completed follow-up; reasons for the seven losses were not categorized.
Arm-specific randomized, completion, and analysis denominators were not reported.
The modified intention-to-treat definition and handling of missing data were not detailed.
No numerical results were presented for glucose, lipids, liver enzymes, muscle enzymes, hematological indices, or urinary screening outcomes beyond Table 2 analytes.
Figure 2 plot coordinates and exact means/SDs for exercise endpoints are unavailable from the printed text; coordinates were not inferred.
No separate quantitative carryover or period-effect analysis was reported.
The trial was limited to adult women with CFS and may not generalize to men or other populations.
The source describes no side effects but does not provide complete event-category counts or a fully specified safety denominator.
The report does not provide arm-specific baseline values for Table 1 or Table 2.
A preliminary five-person CFS report is explicitly unpublished and not part of the randomized trial results.

source_contradictions.details: The converted body labels the exercise-performance chart as Figure 1 in one location, while the native report labels it Figure 2. Native page layout and caption identify the crossover design as Figure 1 and the exercise chart as Figure 2.

The report's measured table outcome is muscle creatine, but the conclusion says improvements were likely related to elevations in muscle phosphocreatine. No numerical phosphocreatine result is presented.
Table 1 prints p=0.00 for reduced activity and mental common score; these are preserved exactly and are not converted to a more precise inequality.
The converted HTML body contains duplicated, reordered, and corrupted Table 2 text. Native PDF table values and row structure were used as authoritative.

The abstract reports muscular creatine 36.3% versus 2.4%, p<0.01, whereas Table 2 reports absolute muscle creatine means and p=0.008; these are complementary presentations, not treated as independent outcomes.

The study is a crossover, but the Methods describes intervention as a between-subjects ANOVA factor. Exact sequence sizes and paired/carryover analyses are not supplied; no independent-arm interpretation inferred.

source_statistical_methods.power: 90% power, alpha=0.05, assumed effect size 1.0; 13 participants estimated for final analyses; sample increased to 21 for predicted 30% dropout.
source_statistical_methods.primary_outcome: Change in MFI general-fatigue score at three months, comparing GAA with placebo.
source_statistical_methods.primary_model: Two-way mixed-model ANOVA with repeated measures for baseline versus post-administration, with intervention as between-subjects factor, when variances were homogeneous and data normally distributed.
source_statistical_methods.nonparametric_test: Kruskal-Wallis test when variances were non-homogeneous.
source_statistical_methods.significance: p≤0.05 in Methods; results and table entries use exact values and inequalities as printed.
source_statistical_methods.table_p_values: Treatment-versus-time interaction from two-way repeated-measures ANOVA.
source_statistical_methods.measurement_processing: First assay reading discarded; mean of next three consecutive readings with coefficient of variation below 15% used.

record.summary: This double-blind randomized crossover trial tested a single 1-g oral acetaminophen dose versus 1-g dextrose placebo in women with CFS/FM, rheumatoid arthritis, and healthy controls. Acetaminophen slightly increased pressure pain thresholds in CFS/FM but decreased them in RA and controls; shoulder CPM improved significantly in RA, while other effects were inconsistent or not statistically significant.

summary: This randomized trial enrolled 91 patients with chronic fatigue syndrome to compare acupoint application plus traditional Chinese medicine foot bath with conventional therapy plus acupoint application. After 30 days, the combined-treatment group had better sleep, fatigue, BELL scores, and cytokine profiles, with statistically significant between-group differences. Six-month recurrence was also lower with combined treatment, 7.1% versus 25.0%.

record.summary: This parallel-group randomized trial evaluated ambulant accelerometer-based feedback added to a combined cognitive behavioural therapy and graded exercise rehabilitation program in adults with chronic fatigue syndrome. record.summary: This randomized trial compared two ambulatory feedback goal-setting strategies in adults with chronic fatigue syndrome: goals based on healthy controls versus personalized goals. Neither strategy significantly changed overall daily physical activity patterns, although personalized goals produced significantly higher perceived usefulness and a significant shift in the distribution of hours relative to the goal.

record.summary: In this single-blinded randomized trial, activity scheduling plus healthcare education was compared with healthcare education alone in older adults with CFS and their spouse caregivers over 8 weeks. The intervention improved Functional Independence Measure scores, caregiver-burden measures, activity participation, enjoyment, and achievement; reported effects were statistically significant for several outcomes, although exact between-group p-values were generally not provided.

source_issues: Table 1 age and education values are internally inconsistent with the prose baseline summaries: prose reports Healthcare Education older-adult mean age = 69.25, SD = 16.32 and education mean = 7.82, SD = 4.29; prose reports Healthcare ED-AS mean age = 70.23, SD = 12.34 and education mean = 7.52, SD = 5.23.
Table 1 prints Healthcare ED-AS education as From 3.5 to 11 years (mean = 7.79 ± 2.06), differing from the prose range and mean.
The flow diagram reports 64 assessed, 4 excluded, 60 randomized, and 56 analyzed couples; the narrative says 56 pairs of couples resulted.
The experimental discontinuation label contains the printed wording '1 spouse caregiver passed away within the first two sessions. of the study.'
The article prints t (59) despite reported analyzed group counts of 28 couples, and prints p > 05 in one instance.
The source reports outcome significance and effect-size statements without providing all corresponding raw outcome values; no unprinted values were inferred.

Eligibility states that both participants with CFS and spouse caregivers should be age-ranged from 65 to 70 years, while the achieved age ranges reported in the narrative are 66 to 82 years for the control group and 67 to 84 years for the experimental group.
Eligibility states that MoCA-HK scores should be >26, but the chapter separately presents baseline cognitive-function values in Table 1; Table 1 values are excluded here per instruction.
The chapter describes a 10-week longitudinal study, while the intervention period is described as 8 weeks following health education in the first and second weeks.

The recruitment flow states 64 couples recruited, four participants failed to complete consent, 30 couples assigned to each group, and 56 pairs resulting after attrition; the unit is alternately described as participants, couples, pairs, and family caregivers.
The reported post-intervention motor-FIM analysis uses t (59) = −0.38 despite reported analyzed group sizes of n=28 pairs per group; the chapter does not explain the analysis denominator.
The same t (59) = −0.38, p < 0.05, Cohen’s d range, and confidence interval are reported for multiple caregiver-burden outcomes.
The text reports p > 05 for the control-group motor-FIM result, while other control-group statements report p > 0.05.
The repeated-measures ANOVA reports F (2,57) = 18.75 for physical functioning but F (2,97) = 18.75 for perceived burden of caring, and F (2,97) = 12.47 for caring activities.

The chapter uses both between-group and within-group claims, but does not consistently specify whether reported statistics compare groups, represent paired within-group tests, or refer to an interaction.
Reported caregiver death is a family-caregiver event, whereas the principal physical-functioning population is older adults with CFS; the chapter does not report patient death.
The chapter reports both caregiver outcomes and older-adult-with-CFS outcomes, and some narrative statements use “individuals” without specifying whether patients or caregivers are meant.

record.summary: This single-blinded randomized trial evaluated combined rehabilitation therapy consisting of traditional rehabilitation, cognitive behavioral therapy, graded exercise therapy, and high-intensity interval training in young women with post-COVID-19 chronic fatigue syndrome. After 12 weeks, the combined therapy group had significantly better fatigue, six-minute walk distance, grip work, and fall-risk scores than the traditional rehabilitation control group.

record.summary: This single-blinded randomized trial evaluated combined rehabilitation therapy consisting of traditional rehabilitation, cognitive behavioral therapy, graded exercise therapy, and high-intensity interval training in young women with post-COVID-19 chronic fatigue syndrome. After 12 weeks, the combined therapy group had significantly better fatigue, six-minute walk distance, grip work, and fall-risk scores than the traditional rehabilitation control group.

extraction_metadata.extractor_notes: Sample sizes were not reported. Table 2 reports endpoint means and SDs, within-arm MD values, percentage changes, and between-group MDs with p-values, but no SDs for change or percentage-change values. The paper text inconsistently labels the grip-work unit as kg.sec while the methods describe grip work in KPa multiplied by seconds.

source_design_and_timing.duration: 8 weeks total; crossover at week 4 where applicable.
source_design_and_timing.visits: Five physician office visits: baseline/week 0 and weeks 2, 4, 6, and 8.
source_design_and_timing.assessment_windows: Rhinitis severity score, Epworth Sleepiness Scale, and daily diary data were summarized from the last 2 weeks of each 4-week treatment sequence, corresponding to the third and fifth office visits.
source_design_and_timing.follow_up: No post-trial follow-up or open-label extension reported.

source_dose_and_delivery.compliance_monitoring: Compliance and symptoms monitored during the 8-week trial; numerical adherence results were not reported.

study_design.treatment_conditions_note: Two treatments within four randomized sequences AA,PP,AP,PA; treatment-condition summaries are not independent parallel groups.

key_inclusion_criteria: Age 18 to 65 years
Unexplained severe fatigue of at least 6 months' duration not alleviated by rest and impairing daily activity by at least 50%
Clinical conditions producing similar fatigue excluded
At least 4 of 9 minor CFS criteria

per_arm.analysis_population: Hybrid Balaam four-sequence design; seven completers per sequence,not28 independent participants per treatment arm
Hybrid Balaam four-sequence design; seven completers per sequence,not28 independent participants per treatment arm

source_participant_flow.sequence_allocation: Seven patients were randomly assigned to each of four sequences.
source_participant_flow.analysis_population: Results are reported for 28 patients; a separate detailed attrition-by-sequence analysis is not provided.
source_participant_flow.figure_completion: Seven subjects completed each arm, N=28.
source_participant_flow.flow_note: Do not infer33 screened or duplicate28participants/3withdrawals into each treatment condition.

source_baseline.eligibility_age: 18–65 years required; observed age range 31–62 years.
inclusion: Unexplained severe fatigue for at least 6 months, not alleviated by rest, impairing daily activity by at least 50%.
Clinical conditions producing similar fatigue excluded.
Both major CDC-based criteria and at least 4 of 9 minor criteria required.

allergens: both types of house dust mite
atopy_testing.seasonal_allergy_handling: Subjects positive for seasonal allergens were excluded to avoid symptom changes due to season changes.

summary: This observational study compared muscle biopsy findings in 74 patients with CFS, 34 patients with myalgia alone, and 22 normal volunteers, with a separate exercise physiology assessment in 12 CFS patients and 12 controls. Histological abnormalities were frequent but varied, and no consistent relationship with CFS symptoms was found; the study did not test a therapeutic intervention.

summary: This observational study compared 35 adults with post-infectious ME/CFS with 20 healthy controls and examined endothelial function using EndoPAT RHI. ME/CFS participants had lower RHI than controls and more frequent endothelial dysfunction, while lower RHI correlated with greater disease and immune symptom severity. In a nine-patient immunoadsorption subgroup, RHI improved at 12 months among those with baseline dysfunction, but the change was not statistically significant (P = 0.06).

record.summary: This longitudinal non-randomized cohort followed 275 adults with CDC-defined CFS, including 49 prescribed tricyclic or SSRI antidepressants and 226 untreated patients. Antidepressant users had lower total symptom scores, lower fatigue scores, and greater reported recovery, sleep improvement, and activity at later follow-up; SSRI users appeared to account for most benefits. record.summary: This retrospective comparative study evaluated faecal microbiome transplantation versus oral nutritional, probiotic, dietary, and lifestyle approaches in 42 patients with chronic fatigue syndrome and irritable bowel syndrome. Improvement was assessed clinically as a percentage, and the FMT group had significantly greater improvement than the oral-treatment group by one-tailed Mann-Whitney testing (U=111.5, p=.003).

record.summary: This retrospective comparative case series describes clinician-assessed percentage improvement among patients with chronic fatigue syndrome treated with FMT or oral approaches. Individual reported improvement ranged from 0% to 95% after FMT and from 0% to 90% with oral approaches; no formal statistical comparison or p-value was reported.

summary: This single-arm follow-up evaluated an integrative, peer-facilitated rehabilitation program in 23 adults with chronic fatigue syndrome. Overall quality of life increased from 13 at baseline to 16 at final follow-up, a reported 23% improvement sustained for up to one year; the repeated-measures ANOVA was statistically significant (F(4,21)=23.5, P<.001), but the absence of a concurrent control limits causal interpretation.

extraction_metadata.extractor_notes: The current report analyzes only the 23-person immediate-program group; the delayed-program control group from the parent randomized study was not followed here. Exact intermediate means and standard errors were presented only graphically in Fig. 1 and were not numerically reported. summary: This quasi-experimental study evaluated a six-month physician-led, multi-component coping and activity-management programme in adults with CFS, compared with a waiting-list group. record.summary: This single-arm study evaluated a six-week symptom management programme incorporating graded exercise, goal setting, education, and problem solving in adults with CFS/ME. At treatment completion, disability, physical fatigue, and mental fatigue decreased, pain changed little, and activity pacing increased; the table marks disability, fatigue, and pacing changes as statistically significant, but the exact p-values are not reported.

extraction_metadata.extractor_notes: Table 2 reports 35 study-two participants. Table 1 separately reports baseline characteristics for study one (n=114), including female 100 (88%), male 14 (12%), not working due to symptoms 60 (53%), mean duration off work 57 (65) months, symptom duration 73 (56) months, FIQ 5 (2.2), NPRS 4 (2.2), CF-p 19 (4.3), and CF-m 14 (3.4); these values were not assigned to the study-two intervention arm. Change confidence intervals for disability and fatigue are reproduced exactly as printed, despite apparent sign inconsistencies.

record.summary: In patients with CFS, adding computerized cognitive remediation to standard CBT and graded exercise therapy was associated with improved subjective neurocognitive symptoms and several objective cognitive outcomes. Objective improvements were statistically significant for Trail Making Test-Part B, Digit Span Backwards, RAVLT proactive interference, and the Visual Elevator Task, although the study was not randomized and comparator neuropsychological data were unavailable.

record.summary: Eight weeks of inspiratory muscle training were evaluated in ME/CFS, PASC, and healthy controls. Reported tables showed reduced sleep symptoms in all groups, reduced pain and COMPASS vasomotor, secretomotor, and weighted scores in ME/CFS, and changes in HRV parameters across groups; exact p-values were not provided in this section.

extraction_metadata.extractor_notes: This section contained numeric data in Tables 2–4 only. Asterisks indicate statistically significant IMT effects, but exact p-values and calculated between-group effect estimates were not reported. Table 3 reported ME/CFS n = 7, whereas Table 2 reported ME/CFS n = 9; Table 4 reported control n = 9.

record.summary: This prospective single-arm study evaluated five immunoadsorption sessions over 10 days in 12 post-COVID patients with ME/CFS symptoms and elevated ANSR autoantibodies. Autoantibody levels fell immediately after treatment and remained below baseline at 30 days, while objective hand strength and neuropsychological measures reportedly improved; self-reported health, fatigue, and symptoms did not significantly change. Statistical effect estimates and most raw outcome data were unavailable in the supplied text.

extraction_metadata.extractor_notes: Numeric data for hand strength, CERAD-Plus, fluency, Trail Making Test B, SF-36, Chandler Fatigue Score, Bell Score, Canadian ME/CFS criteria, and symptoms were presented only in figures or unavailable supplementary tables; raw means and SDs could not be extracted. The supplied text reports no adverse-event data.

record.summary: Eleven post-COVID patients with ME/CFS symptoms underwent immunoadsorption and were assessed before treatment and one month later. SF-36, fatigue, Bell Score, and symptom outcomes showed no statistically significant changes; the smallest continuous-outcome p-value was 0.09 for bodily pain. No adverse-event data were reported in this section.

record.summary: In 12 post-COVID patients with ME/CFS symptoms, immunoadsorption temporarily reduced soluble SARS-CoV-2 spike protein from a median of 207.7 to 22.8 pg/mL among six spike-positive patients. The level rebounded to 207.5 pg/mL after 30 days; figure-only outcomes also suggested transient immunological changes without reported quantitative clinical improvements in this section.

summary: This nonrandomized study evaluated an individualized multidisciplinary intervention incorporating cognitive-behavioral therapy in 51 adults with Fukuda-defined chronic fatigue syndrome, compared with 20 assessed but untreated patients. At treatment completion, 31 of 51 returned to work, 14 were work-equivalent, and 6 remained disabled; among followed treated patients, functional gains were generally maintained, whereas only 2 of 5 untreated patients improved. No formal statistical significance testing of treatment outcomes was reported.

extraction_metadata.extractor_notes: The paper reports counts, percentages calculable from counts, means with ranges, and follow-up durations, but no SDs, confidence intervals, or treatment-effect estimates. Follow-up eligibility differs by outcome subgroup. Table 4 contains merged cells; Table 5 contains repeated status rows. Occupational counts and treatment cost were reported but not represented as clinical outcomes in the structured extraction.

summary: This non-randomized comparative study evaluated Panlongci acupuncture plus moving cupping versus oral prednisone in 72 patients with chronic fatigue syndrome. After two treatment courses, the acupuncture-cupping group had a higher total effective rate than the prednisone group (91.9% vs 71.4%, P<0.05) and higher Bell score (67.29±22.07 vs 56.57±22.35, P<0.05).

extraction_metadata.extractor_notes: FS-14 was described as an evaluation instrument and used in efficacy criteria, but no numeric FS-14 results were reported. Treatment-course timing beyond 7 days per course was not explicitly stated; Table 3 reports baseline, after 1 course, and after 2 courses Bell scores.

record.summary: This matched cross-sectional survey compared 63 twins with CDC-defined CFS with their 63 non-CFS co-twins regarding lifetime alternative-treatment use. summary: In adults meeting CDC criteria for CFS, implemented stepped care in community mental health care substantially improved fatigue severity and physical functioning from baseline to post-treatment. Compared with specialist-centre CBT, the treatment-setting-by-time interaction favored the specialist-centre setting for fatigue and favored the community stepped-care setting for physical functioning; both differences were statistically significant. Improvements were maintained at long-term follow-up, with no significant post-treatment change.

summary: This observational study examined CBT-F in 241 patients with ME/CFS and CBT-I in 162 patients with insomnia disorder, comparing outcomes according to co-occurring severe fatigue or insomnia. summary: This retrospective survey measured serum 25-OH vitamin D in 221 CFS patients and compared them with 103 patients with other chronic diseases and an external British population sample. Mean levels in CFS were 44.4 nmol/L, with 60.1% below 50 nmol/L among nonsupplemented patients; seasonal category distributions differed significantly from the population sample, while levels were similar to those in other chronic diseases.

extraction_metadata.extractor_notes: No treatment intervention was tested. Table I reports means, medians, and ranges but no SDs. record.summary: This cross-sectional patient-reported survey evaluated perceived treatment responses among people with ME/CFS using multiple self-selected therapies. Pacing, oral fluids/electrolytes, compression stockings, immunoglobulin, low-dose naltrexone, and ADHD stimulants showed positive-response rates ranging from 60.04% to 78.70%, but no randomized or concurrent untreated comparison was reported.

summary: This small open-label study evaluated 15 days of oral tropisetron or ondansetron in adults meeting CDC criteria for chronic fatigue syndrome. Improvement in fatigue and capability was reported in both groups, with mean percentage changes of 20.3% to 29.9% for tropisetron and 23.7% to 27.9% for ondansetron, but no formal between-group effect or statistical significance was reported.

extraction_metadata.extractor_notes: Raw VAS scores, SDs, and exact comparative statistics were not reported; several numeric findings were presented only as percentage changes, ranges, or counts. Figures contained additional visual information not numerically extractable from the supplied text. The character z appears where the source note indicates ±, but the surrounding text clearly reports mean changes.

subgroup_analyses.results_summary: The higher-depression subgroup showed significant reductions in depression (t = 4.60, df = 10, P < .001), stress (t = 3.20, df = 10, P < .01), fatigue severity (t = 2.70, df = 10, P < .05), and fatigue-related thinking (t = 2.40, df = 10, P < .04); the lower-depression subgroup showed no significant changes.

summary: Six to nine weeks of cognitive behavioral therapy was evaluated in adults with CFS and compared with cognitive behavioral therapy for primary depression and an untreated CFS group. Overall, CFS treatment produced only a trend toward reduced depressive symptoms and no significant change in stress or fatigue severity, although the more depressed CFS subgroup improved significantly across all assessed measures. Numeric means and dispersion values were available only in figures and could not be extracted from the supplied text.

extraction_metadata.extractor_notes: Outcome values were displayed in Figures 2-5 without numeric data in the supplied text; therefore per-arm means, SDs, and exact change estimates could not be extracted. The paper reports p-values, F/t statistics, and effect sizes of .57 for fatigue-related cognitions and .33 for the CFS depression outcome.

summary: This retrospective, nonrandomized study compared 3 months of oral valaciclovir, valganciclovir, or artesunate with no antiviral treatment in adults with ME/CFS and reactivated HHV-6/HHV-7 infection. At month 3, negative HHV-6 PCR occurred in 37%, 48%, and 68% of the respective antiviral groups versus 8% in controls; negative HHV-7 PCR occurred in 34%, 45%, and 63% versus 7%, with reported P < 0.05 comparisons. Artesunate had the highest reported response proportions, but substantial confounding is likely.

The paper reports 192 study-group cases, but the stated male and female counts sum to 182.

record.summary: This prospective single-center cohort study followed 55 adolescents and young adults with CFS, including 17 with clinically defined cow's milk protein intolerance. Participants receiving a rigid milk-free diet had improved gastrointestinal and systemic symptoms, and their quality-of-life scores improved more than those of milk-tolerant participants, but between-group differences in six-month change were not statistically significant. Baseline quality of life was significantly worse in the milk-sensitive group.

results: Final sample n=187; mean age 36.1 years (SD 15.1); 63% women.
Diagnoses: IH n=63, NT2 n=25, persistent sleepiness after OSA treatment n=25, habitually short sleep times n=41, and sEDS n=33.
Thirty-nine patients (20.9%) met operationalized SEID criteria.
SEID frequency did not vary across included diagnoses: chi-square[4]=4.3, p=.37.
SEID and no-SEID groups had similar demographic and PSG findings, including MSLT-SOL 6.58 (SD 4.5) versus 6.7 (SD 4.3) minutes, t156=0.2, p=.87.

outcomes.name: Source narrative: Subjective sleepiness, fatigue, and scales
outcomes.synthesis_population: Patients with and without operationalized SEID criteria
outcomes.analysis_population: Source-specific groups and item denominators; see each result

results: Overall ESS was 15.0 (SD 5.1). SEID versus no SEID: 14.7 (SD 4.8) versus 15.1 (SD 5.2), t185=0.4, p=.71.
MFI total score for all patients was 71.7 (SD 14.4). MFI total excluding mental-fatigue component: SEID 62.4 (SD 10.2) versus no SEID 55.9 (SD 12.4), t185=−3.0, p=.003.
MFI general fatigue: 18.0 (SD 1.8) versus 16.8 (SD 2.7), t87=−3.2, p=.002.
MFI physical fatigue: 15.6 (SD 3.6) versus 13.4 (SD 4.1), t185=−3.0, p=.003.
MFI reduced activity: 15.5 (SD 3.9) versus 13.5 (SD 4.5), t185=−2.5, p=.01.
MFI reduced motivation: 13.3 (SD 3.7) versus 12.1 (SD 4.2), t185=−1.6, p=.11.
MFI mental fatigue: 15.5 (SD 3.4) versus 14.2 (SD 4.3), t185=−1.7, p=.09.
Mean FSS was 5.8 (SD 1.1). Excluding classification questions, FSS was 6.5 (SD 0.60) versus 5.8 (SD 1.3), t132=−4.8, p<.0001.
Chronotype: evening 76 (40.6%), morning 16 (8.6%), neither 95 (50.8%). Horne–Ostberg scores excluding questions 5 and 7: 39.6 (SD 10.4) versus 41.6 (SD 10.2), t184=1.1, p=.29.
Mean FOSQ was 12.0 (SD 3.3). Excluding question 26, FOSQ was 11.0 (SD 2.9) versus 12.2 (SD 3.4), t185=2.0, p=.048.
Mean BDI-SF was 9.4 (SD 6.8); SEID versus no SEID was 10.0 (SD 6.7) versus 9.3 (SD 6.8), t185=−0.6, p=.55.

results: The average number of medications unsuccessfully used for hypersomnolence treatment was 3.6 (SD 3.2).
Among 165 patients (88.2%) who had tried traditional wake-promoting agents, 46 (27.9%) experienced adequate response and 119 (72.1%) did not.
SEID patients were more likely to have failed traditional wake-promoting agents: 88.6% versus 67.7%, chi-square[1]=6.0, p=.01.
Clarithromycin: 118 patients were prescribed it; response was 37.5% with SEID versus 46.5% without SEID, chi-square[1]=0.8, p=.38.
Flumazenil: 91 patients were prescribed it; response was 64.0% with SEID versus 60.6% without SEID, chi-square[1]=0.1, p=.77.
Medication-response data concern observational prior-treatment history, not randomized treatment efficacy.

summary: This longitudinal study assessed 72 adolescents with CFS who received CBT, comparing those recovered at 12 months with those not recovered. Recovered adolescents had a higher pain threshold and lower daily observed pain at follow-up; between-group differences were statistically significant for both outcomes, with p=0.019 and p<0.001, respectively.

extraction_metadata.extractor_notes: This report is a secondary longitudinal analysis of FITNET participants, not a randomized comparison of recovered versus non-recovered groups. Table 1 reports baseline values for several demographic and clinical measures and baseline/follow-up values for pain threshold and daily observed pain. Figure 1 contains no additional extractable numeric values. External healthy-control reference values were reported narratively: pain threshold 9.8 (SD 1.4), adult DOP 1.0 (SD 1.3), and adolescent DOP 0.73 (SD 0.86), unpublished data.

summary: This prospective non-randomized cohort compared outpatient multidisciplinary rehabilitation plus supportive care with supportive care alone in children and adolescents with CFS/ME. summary: This longitudinal cohort followed 103 people with chronic fatigue syndrome for a mean of 3.2 years after participation in trials of intravenous immunoglobulin or dialysable leucocyte extract plus cognitive-behavioural therapy. Most reported improvement, but only six completely recovered; substantial work, physical, social, and functional disability remained. Long-term outcomes did not differ significantly between the two parent-trial cohorts, while illness attitudes and psychiatric diagnosis were associated with poorer outcomes.

summary: This prospective, non-randomised study compared 6 months of cognitive behaviour group therapy with a waiting-list condition in 67 patients with CFS or idiopathic chronic fatigue. CBGT showed a trend toward reduced CIS fatigue, but functional impairment significantly favored the waiting list; physical attributions decreased and activity avoidance increased with CBGT. Ten of 27 CBGT completers with self-rated improvement data (37%) considered themselves improved.

summary: This quasi-experimental study evaluated a 14-day inpatient occupational therapy programme incorporating CBT principles and graded activity in patients with complex CFS, compared with patients awaiting admission. At 6 months, more treated patients reported feeling better and managing their illness better, while several symptom and illness-management outcomes favored treatment at discharge and 3 months. No numerical means or SDs were reported, and substantial attrition and crossover limit certainty.

record.summary: This observational study treated 1,226 hospitalized patients meeting Fukuda ME/CFS criteria with cervical low-frequency electrical stimulation plus far-infrared irradiation. At discharge, 680 patients were classified as recovered and 546 as unrecovered; recovery of all eight symptoms was strongly associated with ME/CFS recovery, with odds ratios from 2.76 for dazzling to 13.70 for depression, all p<0.001. Because there was no randomized comparator and recovery defined the comparison groups, causal interpretation is limited.

summary: In a prospective before-after study, 32 people with CFS and 18 healthy controls underwent whole-body cryotherapy plus static stretching. Among CFS participants, fatigue, daytime sleepiness, orthostatic symptoms, autonomic symptoms, cardiovascular measures, and cognitive test performance generally improved significantly after treatment. The study was small, non-randomized, and reported no follow-up duration or adverse-event details.

record.summary: This retrospective case series evaluated intravenous vitamin C in 35 patients with EBV infection, including patients with chronic fatigue syndrome. summary: This prospective study compared 16 adults with CFS with 16 age- and sex-matched sedentary controls during incremental treadmill walking, then followed the CFS participants for six months while they received daily L-glutamine or placebo. CFS participants had significantly lower peak heart rate and higher perceived exertion, while peak oxygen uptake and ventilation were not significantly different; six participants showed significant improvement in all five symptom domains by week 26.

summary: This pilot matched 13 people with severe ME/CFS to 26 people with mild ME/CFS to examine potential risk factors for severe disease. record.summary: In this prospective pre-post study, 20 adults with Fukuda-criteria CFS and 20 healthy controls completed a one-month Tai Chi intervention. CFS participants had significant improvements in fatigue, sleep quality, and SF-36 scores, while functional connectivity in the DMN increased significantly. The study was non-randomized and did not report adverse events.

Machine-learning performance metrics are reported but are not arm-specific. Table 1 reports mean ± SD.

record.summary: This prospective pre-post study evaluated one month of Tai Chi in adults with Fukuda-criteria CFS, with a healthy-control group also performing Tai Chi. The discussion reports improved fatigue, sleep quality, and SF-36 health status, with increased DMN and left FPN connectivity; changes in left FPN and DMN connectivity were significantly correlated (r = 0.40, P = 0.012).

record.summary: This six-year follow-up compared cyclophosphamide-treated participants with rituximab and placebo participants from the RituxME trial. Cyclophosphamide participants had higher six-year SF-36 Physical Function values and more frequently reached prespecified function thresholds, while DSQ-SF scores improved substantially from baseline; the SF-36 PF threshold difference versus RituxME was statistically significant at the ≥70 threshold (p=0.024), but not at ≥90 (p=0.10).

summary: This prospective non-randomized study evaluated levocarnitine, coenzyme Q10, and their combination for three months in children with chronic fatigue syndrome, connective tissue dysplasia, and mitral valve prolapse. The combination produced the largest reported clinical effect (82%) and substantial reductions in symptoms and oxidative-stress markers; within-group symptom changes were reported as statistically significant for several outcomes, but no between-group effect estimates were provided.

Of 86 participants who initiated treatment, 40 completed the 90-day protocol, and 38 of those 40 were reported to have significant clinical improvement in fatigue, post-exertional malaise, and orthostatic intolerance. No numerical means, standard deviations, or formal effect estimates were provided in the supplied text.

extraction_metadata.extractor_notes: The supplied full text ends during the Results section and contains no tables or numerical per-arm outcome summaries. Results are described narratively, including 38 of 40 participants with clinical improvement; biomarker findings are qualitative only.

record.summary: This prospective single-arm observational study evaluated 90 days of once-weekly low-dose oral rapamycin in participants meeting ME/CFS criteria. Rapamycin was associated with statistically significant improvements in activity, fatigue, post-exertional malaise, sleep, orthostatic intolerance, several quality-of-life domains, and BECLIN-1, but the uncontrolled design and attrition limit causal interpretation.

The section reports 46 participants completing the full 90-day protocol, while the completer subgroup analysis reports N=40. MFI timepoint-3 p-values are incompletely mapped in the source text.

subgroup_analyses.results_summary: Viral-onset participants had significant BECLIN-1 increases at time points 2 and 3 (p=0.007 and p=0.01); non-viral participants did not (p=0.98 and p=0.69).
Viral-onset participants had one-fold, 0.84-fold, and 2.7-fold reductions at time points 1, 2, and 3, respectively (p=0.01, p=0.03, p<0.0001).
Responders increased 2.6-fold at time point 2 and three-fold at time point 3 (p=0.01 for both); partial responders and non-responders had no significant increases.
Responders had a 1.5-fold decrease at time point 1 (p=0.001); responders and partial responders had three-fold and 2.3-fold decreases at time point 3 (p=0.001 and p=0.02).

Reported correlations included BECLIN-1 versus MFI reduced motivation r_s=-0.56 (p=0.04), BECLIN-1 versus MFI mental fatigue r_s=0.61 (p=0.02), pSer258-ATG13 versus SSS disturbed sleep r_s=-0.63 (p=0.04), SSS orthostatic intolerance r_s=0.71 (p=0.01), and SF-36 MCS r_s=0.59 (p=0.049).

record.summary: This single-arm, open-label before-after study evaluated weekly oral rapamycin 6 mg for 90 days in 40 people with ME/CFS. Rapamycin was associated with significant reductions in pSer258-ATG13 and increases in BECLIN-1, particularly among viral-onset participants and responders, with several significant correlations between biomarker changes and fatigue or quality-of-life measures. The absence of a placebo group and substantial dropout limit causal interpretation.

subgroup_analyses.results_summary: Single-virus EBV patients improved from EIPS 4.1 to 7.0, whereas nine EBV/HCMV patients changed from 4.1 to 4.6.
Abnormal inversions were reported in 61% of CFS patients and 34% of non-CFS patients.
Abnormal flattening was reported in 96% of CFS patients and 71% of non-CFS patients; P < 0.01.
Mean age was 45.2 ± 11.0 years versus 41.6 ± 9.5 years.
Mean duration was 9.6 ± 6.3 months versus 12.6 ± 11.1 months.

record.summary: This narrative review describes subset-directed valacyclovir treatment in Group A EBV-associated CFS, including single-virus and coinfected subgroups. EIPS and left ventricular ejection fraction improved in several single-virus EBV series, with reported within-group significance for EIPS (P < 0.0075) and ejection fraction (P = 0.007), but the evidence is observational and lacks complete variance data.

extraction_metadata.extractor_notes: The paper contains multiple case studies, a placebo-controlled trial summarized narratively, Holter comparisons, and Table 2 demographic rows. The supplied study context specifies one observational intervention arm, so placebo/control groups mentioned within Study 3 were not added as study-design arms. No standard deviations were reported for treatment outcomes. Figure 5 contains additional graphical information, but numeric values were not extracted beyond the text. Table 2 includes 98 overall patients, 21 abnormal-stress-MUGA patients, and 66 normal-stress-MUGA patients; subgroup values are summarized in subgroup_analyses.

summary: This open-label before-after study treated four CFS patients with confirmed C. burnetii infection and 54 QFS patients with minocycline or doxycycline for three months. summary: This non-randomized pilot study evaluated computerized working-memory training in adults with ME/CFS selected for working-memory deficits. Among 9 analyzed trainees, Backward Digit Span and Global Digit Span improved significantly, while Forward Digit Span showed a nonsignificant trend; 12 controls showed no significant improvement. The intervention appeared to normalize converted scores toward healthy norms, but baseline selection differences limit causal interpretation.

record.summary: This cross-sectional questionnaire study compared a self-selected chronic fatigue syndrome cohort with an earlier general medical cohort and also examined litigation-related subgroups. CFS participants who sued or considered suing had significantly different autonomy and satisfaction scores, while the study reported substantial differences in perceptions of doctors and health care. No treatment intervention was tested.

record.summary: This cross-sectional pilot study assessed daily nutrient intake in 24 Australian adults with ME/CFS and compared values with Australian Health Survey data. ME/CFS participants consumed significantly more total fat, selected unsaturated fats, natural folate, vitamins C and E, magnesium, potassium, and caffeine, and significantly less carbohydrate, alcohol, iodine, sodium, folic acid, vitamin B6, and vitamin B12; these are observational dietary differences rather than treatment effects.

record.summary: This cross-sectional pilot study assessed daily nutrient intake in 24 Australian adults with ME/CFS and compared values with Australian Health Survey data. ME/CFS participants consumed significantly more total fat, selected unsaturated fats, natural folate, vitamins C and E, magnesium, potassium, and caffeine, and significantly less carbohydrate, alcohol, iodine, sodium, folic acid, vitamin B6, and vitamin B12; these are observational dietary differences rather than treatment effects.

extraction_metadata.extractor_notes: This supplied section contains Table 3 and related nutrient-intake prose only. The Australian Health Survey comparator is external and is not represented as a study arm; iron and zinc have additional non-parametric p-values reported in prose (P = 0.025 and P = 0.031), while Table 3 reports parametric P values of 0.311 and 0.278.

record.summary: This cross-sectional Australian ME/CFS study examined associations between demographic, supplement-use, and dietary variables and SF-36 physical and mental health domains using multivariable regression. Significant associations were reported for several predictors, including BMI, employment, education, supplements, and nutrient intake, but the supplied section does not provide intervention effects, per-arm means, SDs, or sample sizes.

extraction_metadata.extractor_notes: Source section contains Tables 5 and 6 with multivariable regression beta, t, and P values. No per-arm means, SDs, sample sizes, confidence intervals, or follow-up timepoints are reported. Regression associations were represented as model-based adjusted mean-difference fields because the supplied schema has no dedicated regression-coefficient field.

key_inclusion_criteria: CFS meeting Centers for Disease Control and Prevention criteria
CFS fatigue of at least 6 months duration
CFS substantial reduction in previous activity
CFS at least 4 associated symptoms
Non-CFS fatigue present for 3 months or more
FMF meeting diagnostic criteria with last attack remitting at least 7 days before assessment

Patients with non-CFS chronic fatigue ( n = 20) complained of fatigue
Patients with familial Mediterranean fever (FMF) ( n = 25) served as controls
The longitudinal study assessed 7 patients with CFS.

summary: This study compared fatigue questionnaire scores in 20 patients with CFS, 20 with non-CFS fatigue, and 25 with FMF, and followed 7 CFS patients during a 4-to-12-month course of midodrine. CFS and non-CFS fatigue groups had significantly higher fatigue scores than the FMF group, while longitudinal CH and FI scores correlated closely during treatment. The uncontrolled longitudinal design does not establish midodrine efficacy.

risk_of_bias.key_concern: Dietary adherence was self-selected, and the comparison group consisted of patients unable to follow the recommendations, creating substantial confounding and selection bias.

summary: This prospective nonrandomized cohort study compared 25 patients following a pathogenetically designed health-improving diet with 23 comparison patients receiving the same non-dietary care. Over one year, the diet group had fewer and shorter relapses, longer remission, less additional medication use, and greater restoration of professional ability; the reported between-group differences were statistically significant at p<0.05-0.01.

extraction_metadata.extractor_notes: The paper states patients were randomized, but allocation was actually based on written consent and inability to follow recommendations, so the comparison is treated as nonrandomized. Table 2 reports overall age 35,4±4,78 with M±m notation; the dispersion was not treated as SD. Table 1 contains dietary arginine content values but no clinical outcome data. Table 2 reports overall risk-factor frequencies, not per-arm data: long psychophysical exertion 48 (100%), long stresses 48 (100%), industrial/domestic desynchronosis 32 (66,67%), reduced recovery period 35 (72,91%), occupational hypodynamia 32 (66,67%), abuse of tonics 21 (43,75%), low social-cultural status 11 (22,92%), unfavorable surroundings 6 (12,5%), qualitative malnutrition 32 (66,67%), time-incompatible meals 44 (91,67%), both malnutrition factors 30 (62,5%), and diagnosis duration up to 1 year 6 (12,50%).

record.summary: This retrospective survey analysis examined whether hospital and rehabilitation care addressed PEM among adults with ME/CFS or long COVID with PEM in Norway. PEM-focused care was associated with less reported health and functional deterioration and greater perceived benefit or satisfaction, with several adjusted associations statistically significant. The findings are observational and based on self-selected retrospective reports.

record.summary: This retrospective cross-sectional analysis examined perceived quality of hospital and rehabilitation care among adults with ME/CFS or long COVID with PEM in Norway. Addressing PEM was strongly associated with perceived provider knowledge, symptom acknowledgment, intervention suitability, and perceived benefit, while completion differences were inconsistent. The findings were statistically significant for most care-quality associations but reflect observational self-reported comparisons rather than a treatment trial.

record.summary: This exploratory study evaluated serum SARS-CoV-2 spike protein in post-COVID patients, including 72 individuals meeting ME/CFS criteria, and examined immunoadsorption in 22 ME/CFS patients. Spike protein was detected in 14% of ME/CFS patients and was reduced or eliminated in all five spike-positive patients after immunoadsorption, but reduction was not associated with clinical response; symptom and biomarker severity comparisons were not statistically significant.

summary: This small prospective controlled feasibility trial evaluated five weeks of HRV biofeedback plus usual care versus usual care alone in adults with Long COVID meeting ME/CFS criteria. The reported baseline groups were comparable, with no statistically significant between-group differences in age, fatigue, depression, anxiety, sex, or education; post-treatment efficacy results were not included in the supplied text.

extraction_metadata.extractor_notes: The supplied text ends after Table 1 and contains no numeric post-treatment or follow-up outcome results, despite describing T1 and T2 assessments. The paper states that 18 participants were recruited, while Table 1 reports Experimental Group N = 8 and Control Group N = 9, totaling 17; this discrepancy is preserved.

record.summary: This retrospective matched-pair study compared 15 patients with ME/CFS undergoing general anesthesia with 15 matched controls. ME/CFS patients had significantly lower lowest intraoperative systolic blood pressure and heart rate, but no episodes of severe hypotension occurred; anesthetic management and opioid use were otherwise broadly similar.

record.summary: This retrospective matched-pair study compared 15 adults with ME/CFS undergoing general anesthesia with 15 matched controls. ME/CFS patients had lower intraoperative systolic blood-pressure and heart-rate nadirs, and significantly higher PACU pain scores and opioid rescue analgesia use; other recovery outcomes were not statistically different.
